findings.description: Global color/grade shift between the first and second sampled frames: frame 1 is a desaturated olive-green (approx #756E26) while frames 2-8 hold a much warmer, more saturated golden amber (approx #C89826). The tonal treatment pulses once and then locks, indicating a style/grade strength change rather than any in-scene lighting cue.

result.notes: All 8 frames are featureless flat color fields with no subjects, edges, texture or text, so most taxonomy classes (identity_morph, anatomy_error, boundary_halo, text_gibberish, temporal_warp, object_popping) are not assessable. Frames 2-8 appear visually identical, but with no moving content anywhere in frame there is no evidence of a frozen_patch (a region stopping while the rest moves) as opposed to an intentionally static shot. The only observable anomaly is the one-step olive-to-amber grade jump at the start.

findings.description: Render fidelity pulses violently across the clip: frame 1 is a featureless blue/green gradient with no scene at all, frames 2-3 are moderately detailed, frames 4-6 collapse into heavy blocky mosaic/chroma smearing, frame 7 snaps back to a clean photographic night street, then frame 8 degrades again. The stylistic/quality level oscillates rather than staying constant.

Road surface, storefront awnings and building facades churn as macroblock clusters that shift color and position from frame to frame; the asphalt in frames 5-6 becomes a crawling patchwork of purple/blue tiles instead of a stable surface.

Background geometry bends and swims with camera motion: the right-hand shop row and roofline stretch and shear diagonally in frames 5 and 6, the left building wall smears into vertical streaks, and the street vanishing point distorts rather than translating rigidly.

Pedestrians lose coherent bodies - legs merge into single smeared columns, arms dissolve into color blocks and heads are absent on several figures in the mid-street group (e.g., the central dancers in frames 5 and 6).

Foreground subjects appear and vanish without cause: a large yellow-shirted figure fills the right foreground in frame 3 and is gone by frame 4; a bright green/yellow-patterned bench appears at right only in frame 7; a person occupies the left foreground in frames 5-6 then disappears.

The right-foreground person changes identity between samples - a light-clothed figure in frame 2, a yellow-shirted torso in frame 3, a dark-shirted man with a differently shaped head in frame 7, and another differently dressed figure in frame 8, with no plausible continuity.

Rectangular block regions (e.g., the light grey slab at bottom-center of frame 5 and the mid-left tiles in frame 4) hold stale content and do not update with the surrounding motion, reading as stuck buffer tiles.

Broad violet/blue washes over the road and left foreground are not attributable to any visible light source, and the warm sodium street lamp at left casts no matching warm falloff during those frames.
Illuminated shop signage on the left facade renders as unreadable smeared glyph shapes (green box sign in frame 2, red sign in frame 8) with no legible characters.

result.notes: The sequence is dominated by severe codec-like block degradation that fluctuates in intensity; frame 1 contains no scene content at all, and frame 7 is the only near-clean sample. Findings limited to the listed taxonomy; per-frame flicker beyond these samples could not be assessed.

findings.description: Abrupt global palette shift between frame 3 and frame 4: the flat field jumps from a desaturated olive/khaki (~#75702A) to a much more saturated golden amber (~#C89822) with no scene content or motion to justify the change. The new tone then holds steady through frame 8, so it reads as a step change in style/grade strength rather than a lighting event within the scene.

result.notes: All eight sampled frames are featureless flat color fields with no subjects, edges, textures, or text, so most taxonomy classes (identity_morph, anatomy_error, boundary_halo, texture_boiling, object_popping, temporal_warp, text_gibberish, frozen_patch) have no observable evidence at this sampling rate. The only detectable anomaly is the discrete olive-to-amber color/grade jump at frames 3-4; it could alternatively be an intentional hard cut, hence severity 2 rather than 3.

findings.description: The brown rectangle at center (approx x=313-458, y=222-320) remains essentially identical in size, position and flat color across all 8 frames while the sky gradient, haze level and horizontal streaks all evolve. It never gains the motion blur or tonal shift affecting the rest of the plate, reading as a stalled region rather than an object in the scene.

The brown rectangle has a razor-hard, perfectly axis-aligned matte edge against an otherwise soft, blurred background; the top and side borders show an abrupt seam with no atmospheric falloff, and in frames 1-2 a slightly lighter rim is visible along the upper edge where it meets the sky.

The distinctly darker/saturated blue block occupying the right third of the sky in frame 1 (roughly x=455-768, y=180-300) vanishes by frame 3 with no camera or lighting motivation; likewise the short dark streak at the far right edge (x~690-768, y~185) in frame 1 disappears in subsequent frames.

The two horizontal smear bands flanking the rectangle (left ~x=40-250, right ~x=515-745, y~175-210) stretch, elongate and bow slightly frame to frame, drifting outward and thinning as if the background geometry is being smeared laterally rather than objects translating coherently.

Frame 1 shows a fine blocky/checkered grain across the sky and green field that dissolves into smooth gradients by frame 3, with the green field showing patchy mottling in frames 1-2 that stops churning afterwards.

Overall scene luminance and haze shift monotonically: the sky is desaturated and hazy with a bright band near the horizon in frames 1-2, then progressively darker and more uniformly blue by frames 7-8, while the green field brightens slightly - the ground and sky exposure changes do not track each other.

result.notes: Extremely low-detail, heavily blurred abstract plate (blue sky band, green ground band, brown rectangle). No people, hands, faces or text present, so identity_morph, anatomy_error and text_gibberish are not assessable/applicable. Strongest evidence is the completely static hard-edged brown rectangle against an evolving background, plus the dark sky block that disappears after frame 1. Severities kept conservative given the low information content of the frames.
